# arngz 2.15.0: WP A's empty rule and the window lookup (hv decision 49)

By cc, 26 Nov 2026, for vc and ic, doc before code. Both fixes go on cc/desks1126 over 79cb2c79. Final, after r3.

## 1. WP A's empty rule

**The fault.** `P.empty_by` (plan.lua:551) calls a desktop empty when every id that `hs.spaces.windowsForSpace` lists for it is also listed on another space. That list holds every item macOS calls a window (Hammerspoon's docs: "expect a lot of false positives"). On macOS 27.2.1 every desktop lists system windows of its own, so no desktop is ever empty. hv's dry run planned no remove of the + desktop.

**What r3 found** (sysids/runs/r3-20261126T081250Z.json, one read through `osascript -l JavaScript` and `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(optionAll)`, 56 ms, 710 windows). It still held all 88 ids that only one desktop listed at 08:09Z:
- 41 are system windows, all at a layer other than 0: WindowManager's desktop backdrop (-2147483624), the menu bar (Window Server, 24), a Window Server strip (-2147483602) and the Wallpaper (-2147483625). The + desktop's three ids are one of each of the first three.
- 40 are app windows at layer 0: iTerm2, Console, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp, Teams, Screen Sharing, Parallels, TextEdit and others, unseen apps included.
- 7 are app overlays at layers other than 0: KeyCue, a Safari and a Chrome popover, PressAndHold and LinkedNotesUIService.
- No system window is at layer 0, and no app window that a person places is at another layer.

**The rule.** An id is FREE when the full window list has it at a layer other than 0. A desktop is empty when every id it lists is free or is listed on another space too. Every other id holds its desktop: a layer-0 window, named or not, and any id the read does not hold. ic's point: the read names what is free, never what holds. So a window opened after the read holds its desktop, and a stale read can never empty a desktop.
- Unseen apps' windows are at layer 0, so they hold (vc's constraint).
- A hidden or minimised app window is at layer 0 in the full list, so it holds.
- A failed read gives no free ids, so no desktop is empty, as today. The extras are said, with ic's words: "Desktops not removed: arngz could not read the window list."

**The reader.** opt/arngz/lib/windows.js, run as `osascript -l JavaScript windows.js`. It prints JSON `{ok, windows: [[id, layer], ...]}`, or `{ok: false, error}`. It ships no binary.
- No owner and no title: the rule needs the layer alone. A read without titles needs no Screen Recording permission. r3 ran with none granted to osascript.
- Speed: the read is 56 ms. osascript's start is the larger part, measured at the first run.
- **Who calls it:** the hs side, not the CLI. Two calls: once in observe, before the plan, and once before each removal, so the removal's read is fresh. Each call is `hs.execute` of `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV' osascript -l JavaScript <windows.js>`, with N = 5 s. A hung read ends at N, and it is then a failed read. It uses no Accessibility, so one silent app cannot hang it.
- **The planner stays pure:** observe puts the free ids in the world, `P.empty_by` takes them, and `exec_remove_space` asks the same rule over its fresh read.

**Size:** M.

**Test arms, red over 79cb2c79:**
- plan_test, P.empty_by and the plan over a fake world:
  - a desktop whose only ids are free is empty and planned for removal;
  - a desktop with an unseen app's layer-0 window is not empty;
  - an id the read does not hold (a new window) holds its desktop;
  - a failed read removes nothing and says why.
- engine_test, with a fake `hs.execute`:
  - `exec_remove_space` reads again and removes a desktop whose only ids are free;
  - a desktop where the fresh read shows a new layer-0 window is not removed;
  - a read that times out or prints no JSON fails the removal with its reason.
- log_test: the read's time, count and any error are logged.
- toast_test (ic's): the "could not read the window list" line.
- Live: AC-88504807.7 again. hv presses + and runs apply, and the + desktop is removed.

## 2. The window lookup (arngz.lua:755, 974, 1107 and 2223)

**The fault.** `hs.window.get(id)` is `window.find`, which runs `window.allWindows()` each time: a full Accessibility read of every running app, on Hammerspoon's main thread. One app that does not answer blocks the op and Hammerspoon with it (sysids r1 hung it until hv's restart).

**The fix.** observe already builds an index of every window it can name, as `hs.window` objects (`index_windows`, arngz.lua:239-270). The run keeps it in ctx, and the four sites look the window up there:
- 755 `exec_place`, 1107 `take_hold`, 2223 the step point: the index's window; no `hs.window.get`.
- 974 `grab_point`: the index's window. Its 20-try wait now polls that window's frame until it can be read, in place of 20 full reads.
- **A window not in the index:** the plan places and moves only windows that observe named, so this means it closed during the run. The op fails with "window N is no longer in this run's windows", and calls no `hs.window.get`.

**The Accessibility reads that are left:**
1. observe's one `allWindows` and the window filter, once per run.
2. Reads of one window's frame and app, on the app that owns it.

One silent app can still slow (1), and (2) for its own windows. The bound: `hs.window.timeout(T)` at the engine's start sets Accessibility's per-message timeout for Hammerspoon (the macOS default is 6 s). I propose T = 2 s. Each message to a silent app then costs at most 2 s, and the CLI's apply deadline (ARNGZ_APPLY_TIMEOUT) ends the run past that. Hammerspoon's setting is global, and it has no getter. hv's ~/.hammerspoon sets none, so the value before is the macOS default, 6 s. The engine sets T at its start and 6 s at its end, on every path.

**Size:** S.

**Test arms, red over 79cb2c79** (engine_test, with a fake `hs.window.get` that counts its calls):
- a place, a move's hold and its step point on an indexed window make no `hs.window.get` call;
- `grab_point` polls the index's window and makes no call;
- an op on a window not in the index fails with its reason and makes no call;
- the engine sets `hs.window.timeout` to T at its start, and 6 s at its end, a raise included.

## Order and runs

On vc's word (hv's call): code for 1 and 2, ic's read, one booked bats run (plan, engine, arngz and toast suites, each new arm red over 79cb2c79), and the live check for A with hv.
